title: LLMs Can Leak Training Data But Do They Want To? Evaluating Memorization Propensity in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2606.06286v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models can reproduce training data, but memorization evaluations mostly measure whether models can be made to do so, not whether they do so without adversarial prompting. We introduce PropMe, a framework that pairs a capability evaluation (prefix attacks) with non-adversarial propensity evaluation, and a propensity metric to relate the two. We check every generation against the model's full indexed training corpus with SimpleTrace, an open-source batch implementation of OLMoTrace span matching. We evaluate Comma, its continually pre-trained descendant DFM Decoder, and OLMo3 32B on Common Pile, Dynaword, and Dolma3, with four non-adversarial settings ranging from no prompt to sentences from unseen in-domain sources. Our results show that natural sentence prompts reproduce far less training text than prefix attacks. translated_title: 大语言模型能够泄露训练数据，但它们想这样做吗？评估大语言模型的记忆倾向性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型能够复现训练数据，但现有的记忆评估大多衡量的是模型能否被诱导复现训练数据，而非模型在没有对抗性提示的情况下是否会主动这样做。我们提出了PropMe框架，将能力评估（前缀攻击）与非对抗性的倾向性评估相结合，并引入一个倾向性指标来关联两者。我们使用SimpleTrace——一个开源的OLMoTrace片段匹配批量实现——将每一次生成结果与模型的完整索引训练语料库进行比对。我们在Common Pile、Dynaword和Dolma3上评估了Comma、其持续预训练的后续模型DFM Decoder以及OLMo3 32B，采用四种非对抗性设置，范围从无提示到来自未见过的同领域来源的句子。我们的结果表明，自然句子提示所复现的训练文本远少于前缀攻击。然而，在无提示或仅使用单个常见词的情况下，模型生成的复现量与前缀攻击大致相当。
tldr: 本文提出PropMe框架和SimpleTrace工具，首次将大语言模型“能否”泄露训练数据与“是否会主动”泄露训练数据区分开来，发现自然句子提示下的主动泄露远少于前缀攻击，但无提示或常见词提示时的泄露程度与前缀攻击相当。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces PropMe and SimpleTrace to distinguish whether LLMs can leak training data from whether they actually do so without adversarial prompting, finding that natural sentence prompts reproduce far less training text than prefix attacks, while no-prompt or common-word generation reproduces about as much as prefix attacks.
